hero.headline: Israel orders mass evacuations across southern Lebanon as fighting with Hezbollah escalates
hero.body:
Israel's military ordered residents across southern Lebanon to evacuate as it expanded combat operations against Hezbollah. The evacuation order covers areas south of the Zahrani River, which the military now designates as combat zones.

The Israeli military threatened fresh strikes against Hezbollah positions in the region. The evacuation order affects the city of Tyre and surrounding areas in southern Lebanon.

Clashes between Israel and Hezbollah have intensified in recent days. The escalation comes as diplomatic efforts continue to end the wider regional conflict involving Iran and the United States.

Many Lebanese do not expect that ongoing peace negotiations will bring an end to hostilities in their country. The fighting in southern Lebanon continues despite talks aimed at resolving the broader war.

The expansion of military operations marks a significant increase in the scope of the conflict along the Lebanon-Israel border. Israeli forces have been engaged with Hezbollah fighters in the south for weeks, but the new evacuation orders suggest preparations for a larger campaign.

The Zahrani River runs through southern Lebanon, and areas south of it include populated towns and villages. The designation of these areas as combat zones indicates Israel plans sustained military action in the region.

Hezbollah, which operates in southern Lebanon, has been engaged in cross-border exchanges with Israeli forces. The group maintains a significant military presence in the area covered by the evacuation order.

The expansion of the conflict in Lebanon occurs as international negotiations continue over the wider regional crisis. U.S. and Iranian officials have been conducting talks, though President Trump has said he will not rush to an agreement due to domestic political pressures.

Lebanese civilians face displacement as military operations intensify. The evacuation orders affect populated areas that have been home to communities for generations.

The Israeli military has not specified how long residents will be required to stay away from their homes or what specific operations are planned in the designated combat zones.

cards.headline: Iran restores partial internet access after 88-day shutdown
cards.teaser: The Iranian government has allowed some citizens to reconnect to the internet following a near-total shutdown that lasted 88 days.
cards.body:
Iran has begun restoring internet access after imposing a near-total shutdown for 88 days. The government blocked access to television, chat services, and most online communications during the extended blackout.

Not all Iranians have regained connectivity, and those who have access remain uncertain about how long it will last. The shutdown affected news consumption and daily communications for millions of people throughout the country.

cards.headline: Uganda closes border with Congo as Ebola cases reach capital
cards.teaser: Uganda shut its border with Congo after seven confirmed Ebola cases were reported in Kampala.
cards.body:
Uganda closed its border with the Democratic Republic of Congo in response to an Ebola outbreak that has reached the capital city. Seven confirmed cases of the virus have been reported in Kampala.

Ugandan officials say the country maintains robust disease surveillance systems. The border closure aims to prevent further spread of the virus from Congo, where outbreaks have occurred in the past.

cards.headline: Trump says he will not rush Iran negotiations despite political pressure
cards.teaser: President Trump said domestic politics will not influence his approach to negotiations with Iran, even as the war remains unpopular at home.
cards.body:
President Trump said he won't be pressured by November's midterm elections to accelerate Iran peace talks. He emphasized that U.S. political considerations will not drive his negotiating strategy, stating that Iran is currently "negotiating on fumes" as discussions continue.

Trump reiterated that Iran will not be allowed to control the Strait of Hormuz, the critical shipping route for global oil supplies. While he indicated Iran wants to reach a deal, he stressed the U.S. remains unsatisfied with the proposed terms.

cards.headline: Jill Biden says she feared husband was having a stroke during 2024 debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady told CBS News she was frightened by Joe Biden's debate performance against Donald Trump.
cards.body:
Jill Biden told CBS News she was frightened by her husband's performance during the 2024 presidential debate against Donald Trump. The former first lady said she had never seen Joe Biden perform that way before or since, and feared he might have been having a stroke.

The interview with CBS News is set to air on Sunday.

cards.headline: Iranian state media reports draft deal would reopen Hormuz shipping
cards.teaser: Iranian state television said a draft agreement with the United States would end the naval blockade and reopen shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
cards.body:
Iranian state TV reported that a draft deal with the United States includes provisions to reopen shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and end the naval blockade. The White House dismissed the outlined terms as unofficial.

Secretary of State Rubio said the U.S. would give Iran talks every chance to succeed, a statement that contributed to oil prices falling more than 5 percent. The negotiations continue as both sides work toward a potential agreement.

hero.headline: Trump administration plans to halt international flight processing in sanctuary cities
hero.body:
The Trump administration is developing plans to stop processing international flights at airports in cities that restrict cooperation with federal immigration authorities, according to recent statements from the Department of Homeland Security.

Acting DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin announced during a Fox News interview on Tuesday that the administration is "drawing up plans" to withdraw immigration processing services from airports in sanctuary cities. These jurisdictions have policies that limit local police cooperation with Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents.

The threat comes in response to escalating tensions at a detention facility in Newark, New Jersey. For five days, hundreds of immigrants detained at the privately-operated Delaney Hall ICE facility have participated in a hunger and work strike, demanding improved conditions, better medical care, and faster processing of their immigration cases. On Tuesday evening, immigration officials deployed pepper spray and Tasers against protesters outside the facility.

Mullin questioned why the federal government should process international flights into Newark Liberty International Airport while the city limits ICE operations. "If they're going to not allow us to go out and arrest the 'worst of the worst,' then why are we processing international flights into the airport there?" Mullin stated during the Fox interview. He added that officials are preparing plans to stop processing flights at airports in "sanctuary cities, where the local radical left Democrats aren't allowing us to do our job."

Customs and Border Protection and the Transportation Security Administration, which handle immigration processing and security at airports, are part of the Department of Homeland Security alongside ICE.

The confrontation intensified after Senator Andy Kim was pepper-sprayed by ICE officers on Monday while attending the protests. Mullin subsequently accused Kim and other Democratic politicians of "spreading smears" about ICE and engaging in political stunts.

On Wednesday, the hunger strike continued inside the facility. Congressman Adriano Espaillat conducted an oversight visit to the detention center, describing serious conditions inside. "The food conditions are horrible. We feel that they're not getting medical services. We feel that they're overcrowded, and they're denied their fundamental rights," Espaillat said, pledging to continue fighting to close the facility.

Newark Mayor Ras Baraka has called on the governor to empower the state attorney general to investigate conditions at Delaney Hall. Senator Andy Kim responded to Mullin's criticism, stating the situation was never about personal politics.

The administration has not specified which airports would be affected or provided a timeline for implementation. However, major international airports operate in several cities with sanctuary policies, including New York, Los Angeles, San Francisco, and Chicago. The proposal represents a significant escalation in efforts to pressure sanctuary jurisdictions to change their immigration enforcement policies.

cards.headline: Protests and hunger strike at Newark ICE facility intensify
cards.teaser: Demonstrators clashed with ICE agents outside a New Jersey detention center where detainees are refusing food.
cards.body:
Tensions escalated outside Delaney Hall detention center in Newark as a hunger and labor strike entered its fifth day. Federal ICE officers used chemical sprays and charged at demonstrators gathered outside the facility on Tuesday night, intensifying clashes that had erupted following a day of relative calm.

The protests came a day after ICE personnel pepper-sprayed US Senator Andy Kim during demonstrations. Newark Mayor Ras Baraka called on the governor to authorize the state attorney general to investigate the facility, while Senator Kim addressed criticism from Acting DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin, emphasizing the dispute centered on conditions at the detention center rather than personal grievances.

cards.headline: Justice Department charges Google employee over Polymarket insider trades
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors filed criminal charges against a Google staffer who allegedly earned $1.2 million using insider information on a prediction market.
cards.body:
Federal prosecutors charged a Google employee with fraud for allegedly using confidential company information to profit from trades on Polymarket, a prediction market platform. The employee, identified as Michele Spagnuolo, made approximately $1.2 million through bets related to Google search trends in 2025, according to unsealed court documents.

This represents the second known federal criminal case involving insider trading on a prediction market platform. Prediction markets allow users to bet on future event outcomes, and prosecutors allege Spagnuolo had access to Google's confidential data that gave him an unfair advantage in knowing which trades would succeed.

cards.headline: BBC analysis examines thousands of Trump social media posts
cards.teaser: BBC journalists reviewed thousands of posts from the president to identify patterns in his social media activity.
cards.body:
The BBC's Ros Atkins and BBC Verify analysed thousands of posts made by President Trump on social media platforms. The investigation examined patterns in the president's online communications.

The review represents the BBC's effort to scrutinise Trump's digital presence and public messaging through social media channels.

cards.headline: Teenage rape victim says she fears leaving home after attackers avoid jail
cards.teaser: A girl told BBC Newsnight she is living in fear after teenage boys who raped her received sentences that did not include prison time.
cards.body:
A teenage girl who was raped by multiple teenage boys says she is afraid to leave her home. She told BBC Newsnight she experiences flashbacks and lives in constant fear following the attack.

The teenage perpetrators received sentences but were spared jail time. Their sentences are currently under review.

cards.headline: Paul McCartney releases 20th solo album
cards.teaser: The former Beatle discussed his new album and shared an anecdote about playing guitar with actor Paul Mescal.
cards.body:
Paul McCartney has released his 20th solo album, The Boys of Dungeon Lane. The legendary musician describes the record as featuring "memory songs."

In recent interviews, McCartney shared that he played guitar with actor Paul Mescal, joking that Mescal was the more skilled guitarist of the two. McCartney has also expressed intrigue about upcoming Beatles biopics currently in development.

hero.headline: Court orders customs chief to appear over $166 billion in tariff refunds
hero.body:
A court has ordered the customs chief to appear at a hearing to address compliance issues with refunding tariffs that were ruled illegal. The order relates to $166 billion owed from tariffs imposed by the Trump administration.

The demand for the customs chief to appear in person suggests new concern about the administration's efforts to repay the full amount. The tariffs at issue were previously determined to have been imposed illegally, triggering the obligation to refund the collected duties.

The court's decision to compel testimony from the customs chief represents an escalation in oversight of the refund process. Typically, such hearings are reserved for situations where courts have specific concerns about compliance with their orders or believe additional scrutiny is warranted.

The $166 billion figure represents the total amount collected under the tariffs before they were struck down. The size of the refund obligation makes it one of the largest financial remedies in customs enforcement history. How quickly and fully these funds are returned to affected businesses could have significant implications for companies that paid the duties.

The hearing will provide the customs chief an opportunity to explain what steps have been taken to process refunds and what obstacles may exist to completing the repayments. Courts have authority to impose additional remedies if they determine that government agencies are not complying with orders in good faith.

Businesses that paid the tariffs have been awaiting refunds since the legal determination that the duties were improperly imposed. The timeline for processing such a large volume of refund claims presents logistical challenges for customs operations, though the court's order suggests patience may be wearing thin.

The Trump administration has not publicly detailed a comprehensive plan for managing the refund process. The hearing could shed light on internal deliberations about how to handle the financial obligation and whether any disputes exist about the scope or mechanics of the refunds required.

cards.headline: Amazon signs $6 billion cloud computing deal with Snowflake
cards.teaser: Snowflake agreed to spend $6 billion on Amazon's cloud services for computing chips used in artificial intelligence applications.
cards.body:
Amazon secured a $6 billion, five-year agreement with Snowflake to supply artificial intelligence computing chips. The deal underscores Amazon's push to compete in the chip market, particularly for AI applications, challenging Nvidia's dominance.

Snowflake's stock surged 36 percent following the announcement. The company also delivered stronger-than-expected earnings results and raised its sales guidance, driven by increased demand for AI infrastructure.

cards.headline: Google engineer charged with insider trading on Polymarket
cards.teaser: Federal authorities charged a Google engineer with insider trading related to activity on the prediction market platform Polymarket.
cards.body:
A Google employee named Michele Spagnuolo was criminally charged by federal prosecutors for allegedly using confidential company information to make profitable trades on Polymarket, a prediction market platform. Prosecutors claim he profited $1.2 million from bets related to Google Search trends in 2025, trading with knowledge of outcomes before the public.

This marks the second federal case involving someone accused of using insider information on a prediction market site. Polymarket allows users to wager on various outcomes, including political elections and corporate announcements.

cards.headline: Space stocks surge amid short squeezes as SpaceX IPO approaches
cards.teaser: Rocket Lab and AST SpaceMobile experienced sharp price increases driven by short squeezes as investors anticipate SpaceX's public offering.
cards.body:
Shares of space companies Rocket Lab and AST SpaceMobile have jumped as short sellers moved to cover their positions, with analysts noting the trading patterns mirror speculative activity seen in the electric vehicle sector.

SpaceX is preparing for an initial public offering valued at $1.75 trillion, which could set records for the space industry. The timing of the IPO comes as investor enthusiasm for space stocks remains high, though market watchers are monitoring whether this interest will persist once SpaceX shares become publicly available for trading.

cards.headline: Ferrari's first electric vehicle draws criticism and stock selloff
cards.teaser: Ferrari faced backlash in Italy and international markets after unveiling its first electric car, with investors selling shares.
cards.body:
Ferrari's debut electric vehicle, the Luce model, has sparked widespread backlash. The reveal prompted stock selling by investors and divided public opinion on social media, with memes mocking the new car.

A former Ferrari chairman cautioned that the electric vehicle could represent the destruction of a legend. Analysts have raised questions about whether the model will resonate with Ferrari's traditional customer base, who have long prized the brand's combustion engines and their characteristic sound.

cards.headline: Oil prices decline as US-Iran tensions ease
cards.teaser: Oil prices fell as a temporary truce between the United States and Iran remained in place, raising hopes for a more lasting agreement.
cards.body:
Brent crude futures dropped 6% to $97.43 a barrel, falling below $100 for the first time in two weeks, as markets responded positively to peace negotiations between the United States and Iran. The decline reflects investor optimism that a lasting agreement may be achievable after months of tension.

Trump indicated that a potential deal would include reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a critical chokepoint for global energy supplies. Stock markets also rose alongside the oil price decline, suggesting broader market confidence in de-escalation prospects.

hero.headline: Nvidia commits $150 billion to Taiwan AI infrastructure
hero.body:
Nvidia announced plans to invest $150 billion annually in Taiwan to develop the island into a major hub for artificial intelligence infrastructure. The investment represents a significant commitment by the chipmaker to expand its operations outside the United States.

The decision follows efforts by the Trump administration to establish the US as the primary center for AI development. Nvidia's choice to concentrate such substantial resources in Taiwan instead suggests the company sees greater strategic value in building its AI capabilities there.

Taiwan already serves as a critical location in the global semiconductor supply chain, home to major chip manufacturers. Nvidia's investment would deepen that role by adding AI-specific infrastructure and capabilities to the island's existing technology sector.

The announcement comes as competition intensifies among nations and companies to dominate artificial intelligence development. Securing access to advanced chips and computing infrastructure has become a priority for governments and major technology firms.

Nvidia has not disclosed specific details about how it will deploy the $150 billion or what facilities and capabilities the investment will create. The annual commitment represents one of the largest technology investments announced by a single company.

The move could reshape global AI development by concentrating resources in Taiwan rather than distributing them across multiple regions. It also highlights the challenges facing US policymakers who have sought to bring more advanced technology production and research back to American soil.

Taiwan's government has promoted the island as a technology hub, though it has not yet publicly commented on Nvidia's investment plans. The concentration of AI resources in Taiwan could raise questions about supply chain security and geopolitical risk, given ongoing tensions in the region.

For Nvidia, the investment signals confidence in Taiwan's ability to support large-scale AI operations and suggests the company expects sustained demand for AI computing power in the coming years.

cards.headline: California court allows racial discrimination lawsuit against Tesla to proceed
cards.teaser: A California court rejected Tesla's attempt to dismiss a racial discrimination lawsuit filed by the state's civil rights agency.
cards.body:
A California court has rejected Tesla's motion to dismiss a racial discrimination lawsuit filed by the state's civil rights agency, allowing the case to proceed to trial.

The civil rights agency announced the court decision and stated that trial is expected to begin in July.

cards.headline: Snowflake signs $6 billion AWS deal for AI processors
cards.teaser: Snowflake has agreed to a five-year, $6 billion contract with Amazon Web Services to secure processors for artificial intelligence workloads.
cards.body:
Snowflake has signed a five-year agreement with Amazon worth $6 billion to secure AI chips for its operations. The deal underscores the data warehousing company's commitment to building out its computing infrastructure through AWS.

The contract highlights a growing trend of major enterprises procuring chips outside of Nvidia's dominance. Amazon continues to strengthen its position in cloud services by winning large infrastructure commitments from enterprise customers seeking alternatives for their AI workloads.

cards.headline: Websites can track visitors through SSD storage activity
cards.teaser: Researchers have identified a method for websites to monitor visitors by measuring solid-state drive activity through browser-based JavaScript.
cards.body:
Websites can now track visitors by monitoring their solid-state drive activity patterns. Researchers discovered that simple JavaScript code running in web browsers can detect the telltale patterns of how SSDs operate, creating a new privacy vulnerability.

This tracking method requires no special permissions or user awareness to implement, making it a concerning surveillance technique. The ability to measure SSD activity directly from the browser means websites could potentially identify and monitor visitors without their knowledge.

cards.headline: NASA satellites locate GPS jamming source in Iran
cards.teaser: NASA science satellites demonstrated dual-use capabilities by identifying the location of a mysterious GPS jammer operating in Iran.
cards.body:
NASA satellites designed for scientific research have shown they can also locate sources of GPS interference after identifying a mystery jammer in Iran. The satellites were able to pinpoint the source of GPS disruption signals.

The successful detection demonstrates that NASA's satellite network has capabilities beyond its primary scientific mission. Locating GPS jammers has both civilian and potential national security applications.

cards.headline: Rivian sets June 9 delivery date for R2 SUV
cards.teaser: Rivian announced it will begin delivering its R2 SUV model to customers on June 9.
cards.body:
Rivian has set June 9 as the official delivery date for its R2 SUV. The company previously unveiled the vehicle without announcing a specific timeline for customer deliveries.

CEO RJ Scaringe has called the R2 "maybe the most important thing we've launched to date." The vehicle marks Rivian's push to expand its electric vehicle lineup beyond its initial truck and SUV offerings.

hero.headline: Packers running back Josh Jacobs released from jail after domestic violence arrest
hero.body:
Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs has been released from jail following his arrest on multiple domestic violence charges. An investigation into the incident remains ongoing.

Jacobs was taken into custody and faced several charges related to domestic violence. Authorities have not disclosed details about the circumstances surrounding his arrest or the specific charges filed against him.

The Packers organization has not issued a statement regarding Jacobs' arrest or his status with the team. Jacobs signed with Green Bay as a free agent prior to the 2025 season after spending his first four NFL seasons with the Las Vegas Raiders.

The running back has been a productive player in the league since being drafted in the first round of the 2019 NFL Draft. He earned Pro Bowl honors in 2022 after rushing for over 1,500 yards with the Raiders.

Domestic violence arrests have led to suspensions under the NFL's personal conduct policy in previous cases. The league typically conducts its own investigation separate from law enforcement proceedings before determining potential disciplinary action.

Jacobs' release from jail does not indicate the conclusion of the legal process. Prosecutors will review the case to determine whether to file formal charges. The timeline for any potential charges or resolution of the investigation has not been announced.

The Packers are currently in their offseason program, with organized team activities taking place. The team has not indicated whether Jacobs will continue participating in team activities while the investigation proceeds.

This is a developing story as authorities continue their investigation into the domestic violence allegations.

cards.headline: Tiger Woods will not play in any 2026 major championships
cards.teaser: Woods did not enter the Open Championship and will skip all four majors for the second consecutive year.
cards.body:
Tiger Woods will not participate in any of golf's four major championships in 2026, according to a report. Woods did not enter the Open Championship, meaning he will miss all the majors for the second year in a row.

The decision marks a significant milestone in Woods' career, as major championships have defined much of his professional legacy. Woods has won 15 major titles throughout his career, second only to Jack Nicklaus' 18. His absence from the major championship circuit for two consecutive years reflects the ongoing physical challenges he has faced in recent years.

cards.headline: Phillies pitcher Cristopher Sánchez sets franchise record with 44 consecutive scoreless innings
cards.teaser: Sánchez broke a record that had stood since 1911, surpassing Hall of Famer Grover Cleveland Alexander.
cards.body:
Cristopher Sánchez set a new Philadelphia Phillies franchise record on Wednesday, extending his scoreless innings streak to 44⅔ innings. He surpassed the previous mark held by Hall of Famer Grover Cleveland Alexander, a record that had stood since 1911.

The achievement represents a significant milestone in Phillies history, with Sánchez's dominant pitching performance breaking a franchise record that had lasted over a century.

cards.headline: Georgia coach Kirby Smart suggests SEC could leave NCAA over playoff dispute
cards.teaser: Smart indicated the conference might secede if an agreement on the College Football Playoff cannot be reached.
cards.body:
Georgia head coach Kirby Smart indicated the SEC might leave the NCAA if negotiations over College Football Playoff structure don't reach agreement. His comments came during college football spring meetings where conference expansion has dominated discussions.

Smart's remarks about potential NCAA departure have sparked significant conversation about college athletics' future. The SEC and other power conferences are actively negotiating over playoff access and revenue distribution as they seek greater control over competition structures.

cards.headline: USMNT coach Mauricio Pochettino takes risks with World Cup roster selection
cards.teaser: Pochettino's midfield choices could have widespread effects on the team's performance at the tournament.
cards.body:
United States men's national team coach Mauricio Pochettino announced his 26-player World Cup roster at a nationally televised event in Manhattan on Tuesday, more than 72 hours after the squad was initially reported. The roster reveal brought together the players and hundreds of fans for the official confirmation.

Pochettino's midfield selections represent his characteristic approach but carry significant risk, with potential ripple effects across other positions as the team prepares for the 2026 World Cup on home soil. How these strategic choices perform under tournament pressure will test whether his unconventional roster construction delivers results for the American team.

cards.headline: Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts says relationship with A.J. Brown remains strong despite trade speculation
cards.teaser: Hurts described his relationship with the star receiver as very good amid ongoing trade rumors.
cards.body:
Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts said his relationship with wide receiver A.J. Brown is "really good" despite ongoing trade speculation surrounding the star receiver.

The two haven't recently discussed the trade rumors, but Hurts indicated their partnership remains solid amid the offseason speculation about Brown's future with the team.

hero.headline: BBC investigation finds two women reported rapes on Married at First Sight UK
hero.body:
Two women have come forward to the BBC with allegations that they were raped during filming of Married at First Sight UK, one of Channel 4's most popular programs. A third woman alleged she experienced a non-consensual sex act. All three told the BBC's Panorama program that the show failed to protect them adequately.

In the reality series, single people marry strangers they meet for the first time on their wedding day, though the marriages are not legally binding. According to the allegations, both incidents involved women and their on-screen husbands.

One woman described how sexual activity with her on-screen partner turned violent. She said she repeatedly told him to stop but felt too afraid to report what happened. The woman alleged her partner threatened her with an acid attack if she disclosed the incident to anyone. Lawyers representing the man deny the rape allegation. CPL Productions, the independent company that produces the show for Channel 4, said the woman did not initially inform them about this threat, describing it instead as a passing comment when reported later. CPL stated it took immediate action once the woman indicated she felt unsafe.

The second woman alleged she told both Channel 4 and CPL before her episodes aired that she had been raped by her on-screen husband, yet the episodes were broadcast regardless. CPL's lawyers said the woman had previously confirmed to them that all sexual activity was consensual before making the rape allegation. They maintain they followed welfare protocols and took her concerns seriously.

Channel 4 stated it received "serious allegations" in April against several past contributors, which were denied by those involved. The broadcaster said it removed all episodes from its streaming service and linear channels on Monday afternoon, along with the show's social media accounts.

Channel 4 said it operates under "comprehensive and robust welfare protocols," including background checks, a code of conduct, daily check-ins with participants, and a specialist welfare team. The channel's new chief executive, Priya Dogra, launched an external review of contributor welfare last month to examine how claims were handled and whether protocols need updating.

"I want to express my sympathy to contributors who have clearly been distressed after taking part," Dogra said. She added that based on information available at the time, Channel 4 believed it "acted quickly, appropriately, sensitively and with wellbeing front and centre."

CPL's legal representatives argued that the company's welfare protocols represent "gold standard" practice and that it responded appropriately in all cases discussed. The allegations represent the latest scrutiny faced by reality television production in the UK, raising questions about participant safety and duty of care across the industry.

cards.headline: Early reactions praise Spielberg's Disclosure Day as his best film in 20 years
cards.teaser: Film critics called the director's new sci-fi movie his strongest work in two decades and highlighted Emily Blunt's performance.
cards.body:
Steven Spielberg's science fiction film Disclosure Day has generated enthusiastic early reactions from film critics ahead of its June 12 release. Reviewers are calling it Spielberg's strongest film in two decades, with particular praise for Emily Blunt's performance in the lead role.

The UFO-themed movie has been screened for select members of the press. In a final trailer, Spielberg himself discusses how his perspective on the existence of extraterrestrial life has evolved over time, interspersed with footage from the film.

cards.headline: Olivia Rodrigo responds to criticism over babydoll dress
cards.teaser: The singer said the backlash to her clothing choice reflected how society normalizes pedophilia.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo addressed online criticism of her recent decision to wear a babydoll dress, saying the logic behind the backlash showed how society normalizes pedophilia. The singer said her fashion choice was inspired by musicians Kathleen Hanna and Courtney Love.

Rodrigo recently wore a babydoll dress that sparked discussion online. The singer used the response as an opportunity to discuss broader cultural attitudes. She defended her right to wear the style and pointed to its history in alternative music fashion.

cards.headline: Filmmaker Curry Barker receives eight-figure offer for next movie before pitching it
cards.teaser: The director of Obsession was offered a major deal for his follow-up project without presenting the idea.
cards.body:
Curry Barker, director of the film Obsession, received an eight-figure offer for his next movie before pitching the project to studios. The Hollywood Reporter reported the deal, noting the unusual circumstance of a director securing such significant funding without presenting a formal pitch.

The offer reflects strong industry confidence in Barker following Obsession. Studios typically require detailed pitches and script development before committing to projects, particularly at such high budget levels.

cards.headline: Jimmy Kimmel becomes emotional honoring Adam Carolla at Walk of Fame ceremony
cards.teaser: The late-night host called the podcaster his life partner while delivering a speech at the Hollywood honor.
cards.body:
Jimmy Kimmel became emotional while honoring Adam Carolla at the comedian and podcaster's Hollywood Walk of Fame ceremony on Wednesday. During his speech, Kimmel called Carolla his "life partner," adding that if the phrase sounded gay to some, "it was and it is."

Kimmel and Carolla first met in 1994 when both worked on Kevin and Bean, a Los Angeles radio show. The two have maintained their friendship and professional relationship since those early radio days, leading to Carolla's recognition with a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame.

cards.headline: Apple TV releases first look at Australian thriller Last Seen
cards.teaser: Patrick Brammall stars as a detective in the six-episode series premiering in September.
cards.body:
Apple TV revealed a first look at Last Seen, a new six-episode Australian thriller series. The show will premiere with its first two episodes on September 9, followed by weekly releases. Patrick Brammall stars as police detective Ian Ridley, whose life fell apart under circumstances not detailed in the announcement.

The series was formerly titled The Dispatcher before being renamed Last Seen. Apple TV has not released additional plot details or information about supporting cast members. The streaming service continues to expand its international content offerings with the Australian production.

hero.headline: Trump maintains demands on Iran, threatens further strikes
hero.body:
President Donald Trump has reiterated his demands on Iran and threatened additional military strikes, signaling that despite ongoing diplomatic efforts, military options remain viable. The president's public statements have created uncertainty about whether negotiations will succeed or escalate into further conflict.

Trump set an ultimatum for Iran to comply with his conditions, warning of severe consequences if a deal was not reached by a specific deadline. He threatened to destroy Iran's power stations and bridges, stating that "a whole civilization will die tonight" if Tehran did not capitulate. The White House later clarified that the U.S. was not considering nuclear weapons after Vice President JD Vance's comments raised concerns about undisclosed military capabilities.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards responded to Trump's threats by signaling willingness to escalate, threatening to retaliate "beyond the region" and potentially target oil and gas facilities in the Gulf. Such action could destabilize global energy markets and trigger international economic consequences.

Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif publicly requested that Trump delay his deadline by two weeks to allow diplomatic efforts to continue. Sharif characterized the negotiations as "progressing steadily, strongly and powerfully," though he provided no specific updates on substantive progress. A senior Iranian official indicated Tehran was reviewing a ceasefire proposal "positively," though Iran remained unwilling to surrender its main leverage: control over the Strait of Hormuz, a critical chokepoint for global oil and gas shipments.

Iran presented its own ten-point plan demanding long-term security guarantees, which Trump rejected as insufficient. Iran's leadership, including President Masoud Pezeshkian and First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref, declared their nation was prepared for all possible outcomes and would defend itself if attacked.

At the United Nations, Iran's representative accused Trump of inciting war crimes and potentially genocide. UN Secretary-General António Guterres reminded all parties that attacking civilian infrastructure violates international law. Pope Leo condemned Trump's threats as "truly unacceptable" and called on world leaders to pursue peaceful resolution.

Trump's approach has alternated between aggressive demands and suggestions of flexibility, creating ambiguity about Washington's actual negotiating position and true red lines. He previously stated that a deal would include reopening the Strait of Hormuz but offered no additional details about agreement terms.

The president insists that November's midterm elections will not pressure him into accepting unfavorable terms, asserting instead that Iran is "negotiating on fumes." His willingness to maintain maximum demands while threatening force, combined with simultaneous diplomatic engagement, characterizes his Iran strategy.

Officers in the chain of command face obligations under U.S. and international law to refuse unlawful orders, though it remained unclear whether anyone in Trump's administration would intervene to prevent potentially illegal military action. Whether Trump's approach yields a lasting agreement or further escalation continues to hang in the balance.

cards.headline: Zelensky asks Trump, Congress for Patriot missile interceptors
cards.teaser: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged the U.S. to supply Kyiv with Patriot missile interceptors to help end the conflict with Russia.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky appealed to President Trump and Congress on Wednesday for Patriot missile interceptors to help defend against Russian attacks. Zelensky said Ukraine has not yet built its own capability to produce anti-missile defense systems.

The Ukrainian leader acknowledged that while Ukraine has achieved significant success in defending against all types of drones, the country lacks domestic production capacity for advanced anti-missile systems. The request for Patriots represents a continued push for Western military aid as the conflict with Russia continues.

cards.headline: National Park entrance fees fund Trump DC beautification projects
cards.teaser: At least $60 million from National Park Service entrance fee funds are being directed toward Washington projects ahead of the nation's 250th anniversary.
cards.body:
At least $60 million in National Park Service funds collected through visitor entrance fees are going toward Washington projects as President Trump seeks to beautify the city ahead of the nation's 250th anniversary. The projects aim to improve city fountains and memorials.

The funds come from the Recreation Enhancement Fee Program, which collects money from visitor entrance fees at national parks. Contracts reveal the scale of spending on the Washington projects, which Trump has prioritized as part of preparations for the upcoming anniversary milestone.

cards.headline: Senate Republicans move to unite with Paxton after Texas primary
cards.teaser: Senate Republican leaders are working to mend relations with Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton following his primary victory over Sen. John Cornyn.
cards.body:
Republican leaders are working to repair their relationship with Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton following his primary victory over Sen. John Cornyn. Senate Majority Leader John Thune spoke with Paxton by phone before endorsing him on The Hugh Hewitt Show and criticizing the Democratic nominee.

The outreach signals to major donors that controlling the Senate majority depends significantly on Texas. Republicans are seeking to consolidate support behind Paxton for the general election, aiming to move past the contentious $130 million primary battle between the two Republicans.

cards.headline: Sen. Kim responds to Homeland Security chief over detention protest
cards.teaser: Sen. Andy Kim fired back at Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin after being criticized for attending a protest outside a New Jersey migrant detention facility.
cards.body:
Democratic Sen. Andy Kim of New Jersey pushed back Wednesday after Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin criticized him for attending a protest outside a migrant detention facility. During a Cabinet meeting at the White House, Mullin referenced Kim's complaint about being struck by pepper ball spray at the demonstration.

Kim rejected the characterization that the incident was personal, framing his action as part of a broader disagreement with the Homeland Security chief over immigration enforcement and how protesters at detention facilities are treated.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth travels to Asia amid Taiwan questions
cards.teaser: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth departed for Asia to attend a major defense forum as questions persist about U.S. support for Taiwan.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth departed Wednesday for this year's Shangri-La Dialogue in Singapore, the continent's biggest defense forum. The trip comes as questions swirl about U.S. support for Taiwan.

Hegseth will meet with Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and Minister for Defense Chan Chun during his visit. The timing of the trip has drawn attention given ongoing uncertainty about the administration's policy toward Taiwan and regional security commitments.
